public_sources.title: Scheduling LLM Inference with Uncertainty-Aware Output Length Predictions
public_sources.relevance: Shows heavy-tailed stochastic decode length and motivates distribution/tail-aware physical scheduling rather than point-length scheduling; its serving objective favors SJF/TIE, which is intentionally distinguished here from fixed-prefix evaluation makespan.

public_sources.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Shows prediction-driven size scheduling can be fragile under shift and memory pressure and motivates comparing predictor-based policies against prediction-free/tail-aware physical controls.

public_sources.title: Longest Processing Time rule for identical parallel machines revisited
public_sources.relevance: Provides classical makespan context for why a fixed-prefix evaluation scheduler may benefit from starting long critical jobs early rather than importing SJF intuition from throughput-oriented serving.

synthetic_model.status: Worker-local synthetic Monte Carlo only; not a deployment serving claim.
synthetic_model.statistical_reveal_order: uniform random precommitted order for fixed/two-layer policies; completed out-of-order pairs remain quarantined until the contiguous prefix is available
synthetic_model.latency_model: correlated lognormal, log sigma 1.2, shared latent-task component 0.45, plus independent 1% x10 side stragglers
synthetic_model.predictor: prelaunch X=D+Gaussian noise; lower X predicts shorter pair latency
synthetic_model.two_layer_physical_policy: statistical reveal order is never changed. Current frontier is always launch-priority. Remaining physical slots may choose jobs only inside positions [front, front+32+W), with W in {16,32,64}; predicted-long starts higher-X jobs first, predicted-short starts lower-X jobs first. Physical completion order never determines statistical inclusion.
synthetic_model.occupancy: effective occupancy counts launched pair-runtime consumed up to decision time assuming immediate cancellation; full-obligation occupancy counts full pair-runtime of every launched pair even if decision occurs first.

representative_results.alternative: paired sign q=0.75 independent of latency/predictor

predictor_sorted_statistical_order.interpretation: Not a safe physical-only comparator: it changes which task signs enter the prefix and therefore changes the statistical sample under sign-latency dependence.

predictor_quality_robustness.interpretation: Across the tested predictor qualities, bounded lookahead rather than prediction accuracy supplied most of the occupancy reduction; predicted-long was consistently no worse than predicted-short for fixed-prefix q95 wall in these cells.

null_validity_check.construction: D is symmetric; marginal P(+)=0.5, but P(+|D)=logistic(-beta*D). Fast/low-D tasks favor candidate. Predictor noise sd=0.75. Twenty thousand independent task sets per beta.
null_validity_check.two_layer_pathwise_result: For fixed and all two-layer physical policies the revealed task/sign sequence is exactly the same pathwise because physical completion can delay but never select/reorder the precommitted statistical prefix. With no wall-time-dependent dropping/decision rule, commit/noncommit is therefore identical pathwise to the covariate-blind fixed statistical order; no Monte Carlo approximation is needed for this invariance.
null_validity_check.key_result: Physical scheduling can exploit latency predictions without inheriting the severe selection bias of predictor-sorted statistical inclusion, provided it never changes which task outcomes enter the test or their statistical reveal order.

new_measurement_validity_rules: Use a strict two-layer architecture: statistical inclusion/reveal order is covariate-blind unless the null is explicitly valid conditional on the ordering covariates; physical scheduling may use latency information only if completed results are quarantined until the precommitted statistical prefix is available.

Bound speculative lookahead. In this synthetic model, W=16 retained essentially the same q95 wall under predicted-long scheduling while cutting q95 effective and full-obligation occupancy by about 43%; unbounded/far-ahead speculation is not free even when it is statistically safe.

Do not import SJF intuition from serving directly into fixed-prefix evaluation. When the objective is contiguous-prefix completion rather than mean request latency, starting predicted-long or tail-risk critical jobs earlier can dominate predicted-short physical priority; the serving objective and evaluation objective must be separated.

Treat predictor-sorted statistical order as a different estimand/sampling design, not as a systems optimization. Its large wall-time gain can be entirely confounded with task reweighting and can invalidate a marginal sign-null.
Separate effective occupancy from full-obligation occupancy. Cancellation support materially changes resource cost even if statistical validity and wall time are unchanged.

The pathwise invariance result fails if hard deadlines, timeout-based dropping, completion-order acceptance, or cancellation determine which outcomes enter the test. Those mechanisms require their own validity analysis.
scope_guards: All wall/occupancy values are synthetic normalized-time Monte Carlo and are not measurements of any deployed LLM stack.

The 3000-trajectory representative q95 values and 1000-trajectory predictor-quality cells have Monte Carlo uncertainty; the pathwise statistical-order invariance is exact for the stated simulator logic.
Predicted-long uses a noisy point score, not a calibrated latency distribution or upper-tail quantile; no claim is made that LPT is globally optimal for the actual online prefix-completion problem.
No result extends to GPU memory coupling, side-level slot reuse, preemption overhead, correlated candidate/incumbent service time beyond the synthetic model, or outcome-dependent launch/cancel rules.
The strong predictor-sorted false-commit inflation is an existence stress test, not evidence that real evaluation latency currently correlates with candidate advantage.

frontier.action: Replace point predicted-long priority with critical-prefix tail-risk scheduling: within a covariate-blind fixed statistical reveal order, prioritize jobs by a prelaunch upper-quantile/tail-risk latency score while keeping bounded W. Compare FIFO, predicted-long, tail-risk/UCB-like, and prediction-free age/soft-priority physical policies under predictor miscalibration and distribution shift.

Add a hard wall-clock deadline whose only safe output on expiry is unresolved; quantify resolved-by-deadline, q95 wall, effective/full occupancy and verify no timeout-based task dropping or result selection changes the statistical prefix.

Extend to side-level asynchronous candidate/incumbent slot reuse while preserving pair-level fixed reveal order; test whether launching long predicted sides earlier reduces pair max-latency and occupancy without sign-dependent cancellation.

Continue the separate covariate-conditional inference branch for cases where predictor-sorted statistical order is desired; require falsifiable conditional sign symmetry or explicit stratified/conditional e-processes rather than marginal fairness.

exact_next_action: Simulate critical-prefix tail-risk physical scheduling with the statistical reveal order fixed and covariate-blind. Use W in {8,16,32,64}; compare FIFO, predicted-long point score, upper-quantile/tail-risk score and a prediction-free soft-priority baseline under calibrated, miscalibrated and shifted latency distributions. Add a hard wall deadline that returns unresolved only, report resolved-by-deadline plus q95 wall/effective/full occupancy, and confirm pathwise commit identity whenever no deadline is triggered.
